newsitem.title: CHINA: China lube oil makers hit by foreign competition.
newsitem.headline: China lube oil makers hit by foreign competition.

text.p: China's lubricant oil makers are struggling to compete with a rush of foreign manufacturers, and officials at state giant China Petrochemical (Sinopec) said it was expanding output, the China Daily said on Monday.

Foreign manufacturers operating in China will have the capacity to turn out at least 400,000 tonnes a year of high-grade lubricants within the next one to two years, it quoted Liu Wenrui, deputy chief engineer at Sinopec subsidiary Great Wall Quality Lubricating Oil Co, as saying.
That capacity could even reach 600,000 tonnes, he said.
Chinese manufacturers last year blended 160,000 tonnes of high-grade lube oil. China imported another 200,000 tonnes.
China's total output of lube oils last year was 2.8 million tonnes, most of average quality, the newspaper said.

To boost its competitive edge, Great Wall plans to put a $10 million production line into operation within days, enabling it to increase annual output to 150,000 tonnes, up from 80,000 tonnes in 1996 and an estimated 100,000 for this year, Liu said.
Within the next few months, Great Wall will complete development of and begin marketing a new generation gasoline-engine oil, Liu said.
